claims.text: Tailored heat treatments can increase short-range chemical order in multi-component concentrated alloys.
Increasing short-range chemical order raises local fluctuations in shear-fault energy.
Local shear-fault-energy fluctuations and hard atomic motifs impede or pin dislocations.
Dislocation pinning caused by enhanced SRO increases yield strength.
Enhanced SRO modifies deformation and dislocation-slip behavior.
A disordered or homogenized FCC concentrated alloy can be treated as having minimal intrinsic SRO.
The degree of SRO can be varied by heat treatment without altering overall composition or grain texture.
Localized chemical order creates regions with heightened shear-fault energy that act as hard atomic motifs.
Enhanced local chemical order makes the slip energy landscape more rugged and raises activation barriers for dislocation motion.
SRO and spatial fluctuations in planar-fault energy produce wavy dislocation configurations.
Enhanced SRO raises the critical resolved shear stress.
Enhanced SRO shifts the maximum strength toward smaller grain sizes.
The proposed SRO-strength relationship should hold from room temperature to moderately elevated temperatures at constant strain rate.
Changes in grain-boundary chemistry or secondary-phase formation could confound attribution of mechanical changes to SRO.
In NiCoCr, the measurable influence of SRO on strength may be negligible or masked under typical processing conditions.
TEM and atom probe tomography can be used to distinguish or characterize SRO differences between specimens.
No statistically significant differences in yield strength, dislocation behavior, and measured SRO between the nominal high-SRO and random specimens would falsify the proposed SRO-pinning mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says heat treatment is changed while overall processing is kept constant. A heat-treatment change is itself a processing change; the intended control is more coherently stated as holding all other processing variables constant.

The experiment requires a verified high-SRO versus random-SRO contrast, but the stated falsification rule includes finding no difference in SRO itself. Failure to create the intended SRO contrast is a failed manipulation rather than a decisive falsification of the SRO-strength mechanism.
